subject: Urgent: throttle oversubscription causing 5xx/429 spike — rollback request
messages:
From: Alyssa Green <alyssa@healthsync.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@healthsync.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike: 5xx/429s starts 07:45PT — requests timing out

Hi Naomi —

We started seeing a large spike of 429s and timeouts around 07:45 PT this morning. Our ingest pipeline (project: healthsync-main) is getting intermittent 5xx and 429 responses from your API; client retries are compounding the issue. We have a dedicated capacity contract (deal HS-77) but traffic appears to be getting throttled to project-level limits instead of the dedicated pool.

Impact: several downstream consumers are timing out (30% failure rate on writes), and we're seeing exponential retry traffic. We attached our sampling of request traces and a quick screenshot of your dashboard where bursts line up.

Can you confirm whether a recent quota/tiering change could have caused this? We need an immediate mitigation (temporarily bump limits or move traffic to the dedicated pool) and an ETA for full fix.

Attached: healthsync_request_snaps-20270610.log, dash_429_spike_chart.png

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Green
Head of Platform, HealthSync
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa@healthsync.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx/429s starts 07:45PT — requests timing out

Alyssa —

Thank you, and sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating immediately to our SRE and your account team. Quick notes: we can do a transient quota increase or force-route the project to the dedicated capacity while we investigate.

Next steps I'm triggering now:
- Loop in Marissa (AM) to coordinate an immediate short call and confirm contractual entitlements.
- Rishi (SRE) will triage logs and validate whether the org-level throttles were applied in error.
- If needed we'll perform a temporary org -> project remap to the dedicated pool and do a controlled rollback of any recent tiering changes.

I'll set up a 15-min bridge.

—Naomi

Alyssa, Naomi —

I have availability for a quick triage call at 08:45 PT. Please join here: Zoom link (phone numbers in calendar invite). For context, we've recently rolled a revised tiering policy for a subset of tenants but HealthSync was explicitly pinned to dedicated. We'll confirm immediately whether the pin was dropped by the rollout.

Agenda for the bridge:

Marissa

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx/429s starts 07:45PT — requests timing out

Team —

I've pulled the serving logs and policy audit: around 07:40 PT an automated tiering job misapplied a new default project-tier mapping that omitted the HS-77 pin. That caused HealthSync's project to be evaluated under org-level burst quotas rather than the dedicated pool, producing immediate 429s.

Immediate mitigation performed at 09:00 PT:
- Forced re-assignment of project healthsync-main back to dedicated pool (executed by R. Malhotra).
- Raised project throughput cap by 3x temporarily until 17:00 PT (to absorb retry load).
- Deployed backoff recommendation to the client (please apply exponential jitter; we've shared headers to detect retries).

Observed effect (09:05 PT): 5xx/429 rate dropped from ~28% -> 4% within three minutes and tail latency improved. We'll monitor the next 6 hours and prepare a rollback plan for the tiering rollout.

I attached the raw audit lines and a short remediation checklist.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx/429s starts 07:45PT — requests timing out (executive ping)

Naomi/Marissa —

Thanks for acting quickly. Please confirm:
- Are other HS customers affected or isolated to HealthSync?
- Do we have a permanent guardrail to prevent tiering jobs from dropping pinned projects?

From an exec perspective I want a short note to Alyssa offering a service credit for the window and a clear timeline for the root-cause fix. Also include a one-page runbook for future incidents so we avoid client-side retry floods.

—Vivek
CTO, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa@healthsync.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 5xx/429s starts 07:45PT — requests timing out (resolved)

Alyssa —

Update and apologies again. Summary of actions taken today: 
- At 09:00 PT we forced healthsync-main back onto your dedicated pool and applied a temporary throughput guard (3x) while monitoring.
- 5xx/429 rate reduced from ~28% to <5% within minutes. Tail latency normalized.
- We've paused the tiering rollout pending a postmortem.

Deliverables we will provide by EOD:
- Incident timeline + root cause (Rishi).
- Draft mutual action plan for safe rollout (attached: mutual_action_plan-draft.docx).
- Runbook for mitigating retry storms and recommended client-side backoff headers.
- Service credit proposal (Marissa will follow up with formal paperwork).

We've also opened a HubSpot ticket (HS-77) and attached the logs you provided. Please reply if you need immediate escalation. We'll keep the temporary throughput uplift through 17:00 PT and then revert after confirmation from HealthSync.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
